title: Commonwealth of England
capsule: The Commonwealth of England was the republican government established by the Rump Parliament after the trial and execution of Charles I on 30 January 1649, abolishing the monarchy and the House of Lords and vesting sovereignty in the Commons. The regime faced the conquest of Ireland (1649–52) and Scotland (1650–51) under Oliver Cromwell, who expelled the Rump in April 1653 and replaced it first with the Nominated (Barebones) Assembly and then with the Protectorate in December 1653. After Cromwell's death in 1658 and his son Richard's brief tenure, the restored Rump Parliament and General Monck engineered the return of Charles II, who entered London on 29 May 1660; a formal act of dissolution placed 1662 as the constitutional end of the Commonwealth arrangement.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution.
